title: The Recurrence Threshold for Real-Power Rademacher Walks
description:
For independent symmetric signs and exact real weights j^α, with 0 < α ≤ 1/2, almost surely every nonempty open interval is visited infinitely often when α ≤ 1/4. When 1/4 < α ≤ 1/2, the absolute walk position tends to infinity almost surely.

A Fourier estimate for short blocks bounds joint visits in the recurrence range, including the critical exponent. Conditional first and second moments followed by martingale convergence give visits to every interval. On the transient side, the first hit starts a cluster: an even block of balanced signs has conditional variance of order at most N^(2α−2)ℓ³, producing many expected visits nearby. Dividing expected visits by the conditional cluster size gives the dyadic bound O(N^((1−4α)/6)).

Bhattacharya, Crane and Johnston prove transience above 1/2 under a more general growth assumption and give a dichotomy that leaves the exact threshold open. Volkov independently proves the super-square-root case with related one-time Fourier decay and a local limit argument. One-time summability alone does not give the transient range 1/4 < α ≤ 1/2. The distinction from integer-rounded steps is substantive. The targeted primary-source check through 2026-11-27 located no identical threshold or stronger theorem supplying it.

The claim addresses exact real powers and visits to open intervals. It does not assert infinitely many exact returns to a point or extend to arbitrary sequences of comparable growth.

The exact replay checks 49 balanced-sign variance fixtures, 40 rational exponent fixtures, and the critical equality. The proofs are analytic. The finite replay covers the listed fixtures and the 3D explorer illustrates the worked example. Internally reviewed, not peer reviewed. No proof-assistant formalization is included.

The six files provide the typeset paper, matching LaTeX, bibliography, citation, repository checksums and complete versioned source and evidence archive.

The catalog discovery project credits ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI). The recovered packet carries no per-run model metadata. OpenAI Codex independently audited the mathematics. GPT-6.2 Sol (OpenAI) checked primary sources and prepared the manuscript, finite exact replay and illustrations. DannyExperiments is the project citation identity.
